scope: Keyboard responsiveness, readable help, accessible Options, sender actions, voice pitch, and usable email header controls. This is a beta testing build.

topics.title: Sender actions without spoken email addresses
details: Email message lists now announce sender names without addresses. Missing names are announced as Sender name unavailable. Outlook preserves display names alongside addresses.

Ctrl+Shift+C or Copy sender address copies the focused sender address. Ctrl+Shift+N, New email to sender, or Email sender starts a fresh addressed draft in Subject. Ctrl+N still starts a blank message. No message is sent automatically.

topics.title: Voice pitch and keyboard header customization
details: The Speech category is renamed Voice. Pitch defaults to zero and ranges from minus ten to ten. Use the pitch combo with keyboard navigation and category OK/Cancel, or say Higher pitch, Lower pitch, Pitch up/down, or Set voice pitch minus three. Values are saved. Windows and eSpeak use native pitch controls; AI narration receives higher/lower pitch guidance and its exact result depends on the selected voice.

Email headers are a selectable list rather than a comma-separated editing field. Arrows select; Space enables or disables; Alt+Up/Down move the header. Tab reaches Enable / disable, Move up, and Move down buttons; Enter activates them. Voice Next/Previous header, Toggle header, and Move header up/down work. OK saves; Cancel discards. From, Subject, Date are enabled by default and Size remains disabled. At least one header is required. Header names remain off by default.

topics.title: Immediate navigation and confirmation keys
details: Keyboard navigation interrupts previous speech and discards obsolete feedback. Menus, first-letter cycling, arrows, and Tab use local speech even with AI narration selected to avoid online generation delays. Control alone stops speech; existing voice silence commands remain.

Y/N immediately activate Yes/No for exit, restart, and shutdown confirmations. Arrows/Tab and Enter still work; Escape cancels. Home/End reach first/last items in active lists and menus while editable/read-only text retains its own navigation.

topics.title: Options announcements and readable help
details: Settings on the main menu is renamed Options. Alt+O, keyboard menu activation, and voice Options/Open options announce Options menu through the immediate speech path. The initial focus announcement no longer replaces the greeting. Existing Settings voice aliases remain available.

Help and What’s new articles now open in the read-only reading area used for received email. Character, word, line, paragraph, Home/End, and Ctrl+Home/End keys work. Escape returns from articles through subsections/topics, then closes Help from topics.

topics.title: Beta validation and limits
details: Regression tests cover feedback replacement and interruption order, confirmation keys, Home/End, sender privacy, sender shortcuts, help reading, header toggling/order/Cancel, and pitch commands/markup. Windows integration checks exercise the real native controls and keyboard reading window. Installer checks run before publication.

Live acoustic responsiveness, individual voice pitch response, and keyboard behavior on the tester’s Windows machine still require beta testing. Online AI pitch is guidance rather than a guaranteed exact pitch. No automated check actually shuts down or restarts the build machine.
